pl-l2d35c6-d1e108.summary: Asks whether punishment too is privation or corruption of good.

pl-l2d35c6-d1e111.summary: Answers from the earlier distinction: privation or corruption of good is taken actively or passively, by efficiency or effect; so both sin and punishment are called privation, sin by efficiency, since it deprives or corrupts good, punishment by effect, the suffering that is sin's effect. Fault and punishment differ: punishment is God's, fault the devil's or man's.
claims: Sin deprives; punishment is the deprivation suffered.
Punishment is from God, fault from creatures.

pl-l2d35c6.summary: Asks whether punishment too is privation of good. Privation or corruption of good is taken actively or passively, by efficiency or effect: sin is privation by efficiency, since it deprives or corrupts good; punishment by effect, the suffering that is sin's effect. Fault and punishment differ: punishment is from God, fault from the devil or man.
claims: Privation of good is taken actively or passively.
Sin is privation as efficient cause; punishment as effect.
Punishment is from God; fault is from the devil or man.
